figures.title: The classic view: a thin disk at 80°, Doppler-shifted, with the sky lensed behind it
figures.alt: A thin glowing disk around a black hole, seen nearly edge-on: the far side of the disk appears as an arch over the top and a band under the bottom, and a thin bright ring hugs the black shadow.

figures.title: From 12° off the axis
figures.alt: The disk seen nearly face-on: a bright ring of light around a black circle.

figures.title: From 55°
figures.alt: The disk at 55 degrees: an oval with the far side lifted into an arch.

figures.title: From 84°
figures.alt: The disk nearly edge-on: a flat band with a full arch over and under the shadow.

figures.title: Light going straight: no lensing, half the disk hidden
figures.alt: The same disk with light going straight: a flat ellipse, half of it hidden behind the black sphere, no ring.

figures.title: Light bent: the far side over the top, the ring
figures.alt: The same disk with light bent: the hidden half reappears as an arch and a ring surrounds the shadow.

figures.title: Without the Doppler shift: both sides alike
figures.alt: The disk without the Doppler shift: both sides the same brightness.

figures.title: The photon ring, close
figures.alt: A close view of the photon ring: a thin bright circle on the edge of the shadow, the disk behind.

figures.title: A star field, lensed
figures.alt: A star field seen through a black hole: stars smeared into arcs around a circular shadow, a bright Einstein ring.

figures.title: The same star field, not lensed
figures.alt: The same star field with light going straight: only a black circle blocks the stars.

figures.title: A recomputation of Luminet's 1979 picture, drawn as ink dots
figures.alt: Black ink dots on white paper, denser where the disk is brighter: the disk, its arch over the top, its band underneath, and the thin ring.

figures.title: Wide, from 70°
figures.alt: A wide dark view of the disk from above.
